name: LongBench v2
ability_definition: The ability to read and understand information and ideas presented in writing.

task_realism.reasoning: Many contexts are real documents that workers actually read: academic papers, legal texts, financial reports, government documents, novels and dialogue logs. Expert-written questions require understanding, inference and cross-document synthesis rather than surface lookup. However, the code-repository and structured-data categories exercise skills beyond prose reading. The extreme lengths (up to ~2M words in a single pass) are also atypical of most workplace reading.

evaluation_conditions.reasoning: The input distribution is fairly authentic, and questions were filtered so they cannot be answered from memorized knowledge alone, which matches the real need to understand the given text. Several conditions differ from real work, though. The whole corpus arrives in one prompt with no tools, search, re-reading strategy or ability to ask clarifying questions. There are no stakes. Workplace readers usually have a purpose-driven task rather than a pre-posed question.

construct_coverage.reasoning: It covers main-idea, detail, inference and multi-part relational understanding across varied genres. Coverage is still partial. It is dominated by long-context retrieval and reasoning, and it underrepresents the short-to-medium texts that make up most everyday workplace reading. Code and table tasks dilute its focus on prose. With only 503 items, breadth across genres and question types is limited.

format_match.reasoning: The inputs are realistic documents, but the output is a forced choice among four options. Real comprehension shows up as summaries, answers, decisions or actions based on the text. Multiple choice also allows elimination strategies and does not test whether the model can state its understanding in its own words.

transferability_reasoning: LongBench v2 uses authentic, varied documents and hard expert questions that resist memorization, which gives it moderate relevance to real-world reading comprehension. Its transfer is limited by the multiple-choice output format, the emphasis on extreme-length retrieval over typical reading, and the inclusion of code and structured-data tasks outside prose comprehension. It is a reasonable but partial proxy for workplace written comprehension.

2025.metric: accuracy (%) on the full 503-question multiple-choice set
2025.human_reference: Relevant educated workforce: college-educated professionals who read and analyze long documents (reports, contracts, codebases, data) at work. The published baseline comes from a comparable or slightly stronger group (domain-knowledgeable annotators).

2026.metric: accuracy (%), overall across 503 multiple-choice questions (reported by the source as 0.663 on a 0-1 scale)
2026.human_reference: Relevant educated workforce: college-educated professionals who read and synthesize long documents at work, such as analysts, researchers, legal and policy staff.
